clue.text: Grant county the final Test

parts.note: to show mercy or favour is to grant it, an old sense of show
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A cricket report on the last Test match in a series, played somewhere in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland. The definition takes 'Test' loosely as any decisive trial, not only a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is the decisive confrontation that settles a contest, the last and deciding trial.

clue.text: Magnificent European going around on horseback

indicators.note: the European is said to go around, so his letters enclose the riding piece

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia
a rider who is up is mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: A splendid sight: a continental gentleman out riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym for splendid or outstandingly fine.

clue.text: Tramp loses his hat first — he's in the wind

indicators.note: a hat sits on top, so losing it means the opening letter, his initial H, goes

parts.note: a hobo is an American tramp
the suffix -ist names a person who does something, so it stands for he's

explanation.surface: A vagrant whose hat blows off in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' means playing in the woodwind section of an orchestra; the old spelling hoboist for this player makes the tramp a natural start.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe belongs to the woodwind, so its player sits among the wind instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Retainer of French ornament.

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a pendant is a hanging ornament on a necklace

explanation.surface: A servant belonging to a piece of French jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a servant or follower who relies on a household, a dependent person.

clue.text: Mad royal rebel worthy of this fruit

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch decides that a rebel deserves a particular berry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' shuffles R (royal) with REBEL and WORTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: The whortleberry is the bilberry, a small blue-black edible berry of heathland shrubs.

clue.text: Wit of the impish fellow beginning with his conclusion!

indicators.note: the fellow's final letter is shifted so that it starts the word instead

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous elf or impish spirit

explanation.surface: Praise for the humour of a mischievous man who starts with his punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning with his conclusion' moves the last letter E of SPRITE to the front, giving ESPRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively intelligence and sparkle, borrowed from French, close to cleverness in talk.

clue.text: Female has a record as a parishioner

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman of the parish who has made a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative: a congregation is the vicar's flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor tends his flock, so a member of a parish congregation is figuratively one of the flock.

clue.text: Shy about dressing in the theatre?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
tiring is an old word for dressing, as in a theatre's tiring-room

explanation.surface: A bashful actor uneasy about changing costume backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiring-room was the dressing room of an Elizabethan theatre, from attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is reserved and avoids company, bashful by nature.

clue.text: Note about Republican states makes us cross

indicators.note: the note goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
avers means states or asserts

explanation.surface: A political memo about Republican claims annoys us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective (annoyed) but is the verb: to cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse land is to travel across it from one side to the other.

clue.text: Scornfully dismiss band twice rejected

indicators.note: twice says the turned piece appears two times in a row
rejected means sent back, so the band is read backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: A music fan twice turns down the same group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns HOOP into POOH, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to wave it away with contempt, treating it as unworthy.

clue.text: Bunk with a woman!

parts.note: a berth is a bunk on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about sharing a bed with a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's name.

clue.text: Cover for student involved in track activity

indicators.note: the student is placed within the track activity

parts.note: pacesetting is the job of a runner who leads to set the speed in a race
L is the learner plate, standing for student

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for a student who was busy with athletics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is the restaurant sense: each diner's set of cutlery and glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: In a restaurant a cover is one diner's laid place of cutlery, plates and glasses.

clue.text: Got up in a sari sent from Bombay

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in a sari that was posted from India.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies across 'saRI SENt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen is the past participle of rise, so it matches got up in the sense of having stood.

clue.text: It has branches in America for the manufacture of turtle pie

indicators.note: manufacture means making something new from the materials, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American recipe calling for turtle meat baked in pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the manufacture of' rearranges TURTLE PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip tree is a tall North American tree of the magnolia family, so a thing with branches there.

clue.text: Unusual inns, even lace found here

definitions.text: Unusual inns, even lace found here

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller notes odd hostelries and even lacework in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges INNS EVEN LACE; the whole clue then points to the French town famous for lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Valenciennes is a town in northern France that gave its name to a fine bobbin lace.

clue.text: Stand up, prepare the way, make a speech, and disappear

indicators.note: in a down entry standing up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pave the way is to prepare it
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Instructions for a politician: rise, clear a path, speak, then vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' turns PAVE upwards in this down entry, giving EVAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn to vapour, and so figuratively to vanish.

clue.text: Branch temporarily not wanting sporting activity

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's taste for it for now
a shoot is a hunting outing with guns

explanation.surface: A person who has gone off country sports for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A shoot is a day's game shooting, a country sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side growth from a plant's stem, a sprout or limb.

clue.text: Overriding instruction not to trap a bird

indicators.note: trapping puts the bird inside, so the instruction's letters surround it

parts.note: an instruction not to do something is a don't
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A firm order forbidding anyone to catch a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trap' puts the bird inside; mina is an older spelling of myna, the talking starling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominant means prevailing over all others, the ruling or chief influence.

clue.text: TV presenter accepts new rise, being on the borderline

indicators.note: the presenter takes in the other piece, holding it within his letters

parts.note: a frontman presents a television programme

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the word rise is reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A television host gets a fresh pay rise but is only just keeping his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the rise into IERS and 'accepts' sets it inside the presenter; a frontman is a show's on-screen host.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontiersman lives at the edge of settled territory, out by the border.

clue.text: Text of play for West End requiring a certificate first

indicators.note: first says the certificate comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: scrip is a certificate, for instance of shares

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A West End theatre production that needs a licence before opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatreland but gives the last letter of West, T; 'first' puts SCRIP before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written words of a play, the actors' lines on the page.

clue.text: It's cold in a large lorry here!

definitions.text: It's cold in a large lorry here!

indicators.note: in puts the cold piece inside the lorry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trucker complains of the chill in the cab of his articulated lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is British shorthand for an articulated lorry; the whole clue also describes the polar region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the frozen polar region at the top of the globe, notoriously freezing.

clue.text: Filament-forming device sited outside a Greater London town

indicators.note: outside means the one word is placed around the other

parts.note: set means placed or sited
Pinner is a suburb in north-west Greater London

explanation.surface: A machine for making threads has been placed on the edge of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in the London borough of Harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ a spider or silkworm uses to extrude silk, or the nozzle doing the same for synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Loop or ring where a savage may have it.

indicators.note: the nose is said to have the ring in it, enclosing that letter

parts.note: a nose ring is the old cartoon image of a so-called savage
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An old adventure-story picture of a tribesman with a ring through his nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring, O, goes into the NOSE that the savage wears it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Award for building an old-style vehicle

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the calendar before 1752
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A prize for restoring a vintage motor.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Style (OS) marks dates in the Julian calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: One speaking in a small chapel, mostly?

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter of the chapel is dropped

parts.note: an oratory is a small chapel for private prayer

explanation.surface: A preacher holding forth in a little chapel, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ORATORY to its first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, one who delivers speeches.

clue.text: Contestant unfortunately slain in sudden attack

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the attack

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack of illness

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the word slain is jumbled

explanation.surface: A competitor sadly killed in a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' gives INALS and 'in' sets it within the attack; the surface's killing is a red herring for a sporting finalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist is a competitor who has reached the deciding round.

clue.text: Row about race causes a laugh

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the race

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A squabble over a race prompts some giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man's Tourist Trophy motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a suppressed nervous giggle.

clue.text: Its grace may be rural

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a lord's refinement is just countrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges ITS GRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrestic means of the fields or countryside, rustic.
